title: Micro-extraction method for analysis of flame retardants in dust from HVAC air filters
author: Schachterle, Lowe, et al.
materials: Stock solutions of the organophosphate ester (OPE) flame retardants including 510 ng/µL (TCPP) and 860 ng/µL TDCPP, 1020 ng/µL TPHP, 978 ng/µL T24DtBPP and 980 ng/µL HMB, the internal standard (IS), were prepared in 25.00 mL of hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v) via volumetric flask. (Note: these final concentrations reflect the % purity of the original chemical purchased in Standards, solvents, and materials). Stock solutions were prepared every six months. These individual stock solutions were used to prepare 25.00 mL of a working stock solution containing 10 ng/µL TCPP, TDCPP, TPHP, and T24DtBPP in hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v) via volumetric flask. Separate HMB working stock solutions with concentrations of 10 ng/µL and 0.13 ng/µL were prepared in hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v). The working stock solution of the OPE mix at 10 ng/µL and the HMB IS were used to prepare analytical standards to generate calibration curves (Table 1), and these working stock solutions were prepared every two months. All calibration standards contained a final volume of 0.050 ng/µL HMB. Stocks, working stocks, and analytical calibration standards were stored in glass vials at 3.5°C when not in use.Table 1Volumes of solvent and working stock solutions to prepare analytical calibration standards for analysis of selected OPEs by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC/MS). All analytical standards contained a final volume of 0.0500 ng/µL HMB, which was added as internal standard (IS).Table 1:Concentration of OPEs (ng/µL)Volume of Hexane/Acetone (50/50, v/v), µLVolume of OPEs Working Stock (10 ng/µL), µLVolume of HMB Working Stock (10.0 ng/µL), µL1.0900.100.5.00.52900.50.5.00.241000.25.5.00.101000.10.5.00.0501000.5.05.00.0101000.1.05.0

A stock solution of 1350 mg/L of TBBPA in methanol was prepared in a 25.00 mL volumetric flask. TriBBPA was synthesized as described (see Synthesis and characterization of TriBBPA), and a stock solution of 1190 ng/µL TriBBPA in methanol (25.00 mL) was prepared from this synthesized and characterized product. Two working stock solutions containing TBBPA and TriBBPA in methanol (25.00 mL) at 1.0 ng/µL and 10 ng/µL were prepared from the stock solutions, and these working stock solutions were prepared every two months. The 10 ng/µL working stock solution was used for preparing the analytical standards (Table 2). An aliquot of ammonium hydroxide was added to all analytical standards to assist in ionization of the compounds via electrospray ionization (ESI). The stocks, working stocks, and analytical standards of the two BFRs were stored in glass vials at 3.5°C when not in use.Table 2Volumes of solvent and working stock solutions to prepare analytical calibration standards for analysis of TBBPA and its derivative, TriBBPA, by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC/MS).Table 2:Concentration of BFRs (ng/µL)Volume of Methanol µLVolume of BFRs Working Stock (10 ng/µL), µLVolume of NH4OH, µL1.0900.100.5.00.52900.50.5.00.241000.25.5.00.101000.10.5.00.0501000.5.05.0

When the analyte class included the BFRs for analysis by LC/MS, 200 µL of the dust extract were added to a 300 µL PolySpring® insert. These glass inserts were placed in a plastic microcentrifuge vial and centrifuged at 14,700 rpm for 30 min (Thermo Scientific Legend 17 centrifuge). The supernatant was transferred to a clean insert, leaving any particulates behind that may have clogged the PEEK lines of the LC/MS. The insert containing the centrifuged extract was placed in a screw-top autosampler vial and analyzed via LC/MS (see Instrumentation and analysis of BFRs – LC/MS for details).

steps.title: Prepare OPE stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each organophosphate ester (OPE) flame retardant in 25.00 mL of hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v) in a volumetric flask to obtain the following concentrations: TCPP 510 ng/µL, TDCPP 860 ng/µL, TPHP 1020 ng/µL, T24DtBPP 978 ng/µL, and the internal standard HMB 980 ng/µL. Record that stock solutions are prepared every six months and stored in glass vials at 3.5 °C when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare OPE working stock and calibration standards
steps.instruction: Combine the individual OPE stock solutions to make a 25.00 mL working stock containing 10 ng/µL each of TCPP, TDCPP, TPHP, and T24DtBPP in hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v). Prepare separate HMB working stocks at 10 ng/µL and 0.13 ng/µL in the same solvent. Using these working stocks, prepare analytical calibration standards (Table 1) so that each standard contains a final HMB concentration of 0.050 ng/µL. The volumes for each concentration level are:

substeps.instruction: 1.0 ng/µL: 900 µL solvent, 100 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.
0.5 ng/µL: 900 µL solvent, 50 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.
0.25 ng/µL: 1000 µL solvent, 25 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.
0.10 ng/µL: 1000 µL solvent, 10 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.
0.05 ng/µL: 1000 µL solvent, 5 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.
0.01 ng/µL: 1000 µL solvent, 1 µL OPE working stock, 0.5 µL HMB working stock.

steps.title: Prepare BFR stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make a 25.00 mL stock solution of TBBPA at 1350 mg/L in methanol. Synthesize TriBBPA as described elsewhere and prepare a 25.00 mL stock of TriBBPA at 1190 ng/µL in methanol.

steps.title: Prepare BFR working stocks and calibration standards
steps.instruction: From the TBBPA and TriBBPA stock solutions prepare two methanol working stocks (25 mL each) at 1.0 ng/µL and 10 ng/µL. Use the 10 ng/µL working stock to prepare calibration standards (Table 2) with the following volumes for each concentration level, adding an aliquot of ammonium hydroxide to each standard to aid ESI ionisation:

substeps.instruction: 1.0 ng/µL: 900 µL methanol, 100 µL BFR working stock, 0.5 µL NH4OH.
0.5 ng/µL: 900 µL methanol, 50 µL BFR working stock, 0.5 µL NH4OH.
0.25 ng/µL: 1000 µL methanol, 25 µL BFR working stock, 0.5 µL NH4OH.
0.10 ng/µL: 1000 µL methanol, 10 µL BFR working stock, 0.5 µL NH4OH.
0.05 ng/µL: 1000 µL methanol, 5 µL BFR working stock, 0.5 µL NH4OH.

steps.title: Extract dust sample
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 25 mg of sieved HVAC filter dust into a silanized glass culture tube on a Mettler Toledo XS64 analytical balance and record the exact weight. Add 1.0 mL hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v), cap with a Teflon‑lined cap, vortex for 1 min, sonicate in an ultrasonic water bath for 10 min at 25–30 °C, then centrifuge on a Fisher Scientific FS20 for 15 min (or until the dust pellet is clear).

steps.title: Prepare GC/MS injection for OPEs
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, transfer 10 µL of the dust extract, 20 µL of the 0.13 ng/µL HMB internal‑standard solution, and 20 µL of hexane/acetone (50/50, v/v) into a 350 µL pulled‑point glass insert placed in a crimp‑top autosampler vial. Vortex the vial for 10 s and place it on the GC/MS autosampler tray for analysis.

steps.title: Centrifuge extract for BFR LC/MS analysis
steps.instruction: If the analyte class includes BFRs, add 200 µL of the dust extract to a 300 µL PolySpring® insert, place the insert in a plastic microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 14,700 rpm for 30 min using a Thermo Scientific Legend 17. Transfer the clear supernatant to a clean insert, leaving particulates behind, then place the insert in a screw‑top autosampler vial for LC/MS injection.

steps.title: Run GC/MS analysis for OPEs
steps.instruction: Use a Hewlett‑Packard 6890 GC coupled to a 5973 MSD. Install an HP‑5MS column (25 m × 0.200 mm, 0.33 µm film). Set hydrogen carrier gas pressure to 5.05 psi (0.7 mL/min). Set inlet temperature to 250 °C in split/splitless mode. Inject 1.0 µL of sample, standard, or blank. Program the oven: start at 60 °C (hold 3.00 min), ramp to 305 °C at 30.00 °C/min, hold 13.00 min (total run 24.17 min).

steps.title: Set GC/MS MSD SIM parameters
steps.instruction: Operate the MSD in selected‑ion monitoring (SIM) mode with four acquisition windows. Set transfer line to 280 °C, source to 230 °C, quadrupole to 150 °C. Set electron multiplier 200 V above tune voltage. Define acquisition windows: 7.0–9.5 min for HMB (quant ion m/z 147.1, confirm 117.0), 9.0–9.5 min for TCPP (m/z 277.0, confirm 101.0, 279.0), 10.9–11.5 min for TDCPP (m/z 381.0, confirm 191.0, 209.0, 383.0), 11.1–12.0 min for TPHP (m/z 326.0, confirm 215.0, 233.0, 325.0), 19.1–24.1 min for T24DtBPP (m/z 647.5, confirm 462.4, 662.5, 363.5).

steps.title: Run LC/MS analysis for BFRs
steps.instruction: Use a Shimadzu LCMS‑8030 with an XBridge C18 column (50 × 2.1 mm, 3.5 µm). Mobile phase A: 18 MΩ water with 0.1 % (v/v) NH4OH and 2.5 mM ammonium formate (pH ≈ 9). Mobile phase B: Optima LC/MS‑grade methanol with 0.2 % (v/v) NH4OH and 2.5 mM ammonium formate (pH 8–8.5). Set flow rate to 0.4000 mL/min, column oven to 40 °C, injection volume 5.0 µL. Gradient: 0 min 5 % B (hold 2.0 min), increase to 80 % B (hold until 5.0 min), return to 5 % B at 5.1 min (hold 2.9 min) for a total run time of 8.0 min.

steps.title: Set LC/MS ESI parameters
steps.instruction: Operate the electrospray source in negative‑ion mode. Set desolvation temperature to 250 °C. Set nebulizing N₂ gas flow to 1.50 L/min and drying N₂ gas flow to 15.00 L/min. Use selected‑ion monitoring (SIM) for quantitation with a dwell time of 38.0 ms. Monitor the following SIM ions: TBBPA (quant 542.8 m/z, confirm 544.8 m/z, 540.7 m/z) and TriBBPA (quant 462.8 m/z, confirm 460.9 m/z, 466.8 m/z).

steps.title: Store extracts and clean equipment
steps.instruction: Analyze all extracts on the same day of preparation. Store any remaining extract in crimp‑top glass vials at 3.5 °C for possible re‑analysis. Triple‑rinse the silanized glass culture tubes with acetone then de‑ionised water, and bake them in a GC oven at 250 °C for 30 min before reuse.
